sector_model: insurer (Florida homeowners P&C, reciprocal-style reinsurance dependent); use earnings, book value, reserves, catastrophe and reinsurance; no FCF model
thesis: HCI Group (Florida-focused property insurer) reported nine-month 2026 net income of 230.7M (vs 201.4M), diluted EPS 17.48, equity 1,121.3M and small debt (31.8M carrying amount). At 186.03 it trades near 7.0x TTM net income (7.5x TTM diluted EPS of 24.73) and 2.1x book, a low multiple for that earnings level, with 80.0M of 2026 buybacks. Update 2026-11-09 12:20 ET: 10-Q text read. Net combined ratio 58.8% (9M), no 2026 catastrophe losses, ceded cost down to 30.7% of gross premiums after the 2026-27 reinsurance renewal.
counterthesis: A single-state hurricane exposure can erase several years of earnings, and a low P/E on peak profits is typical for property insurers late in a favorable cat cycle. Net premiums earned are only +12.6% in 9M26 vs a year earlier and flat sequentially (219.1M Q3 vs 219.0M Q2); unearned premiums rose, but cash and equivalents fell from 1,210M to 744M (partly to buybacks and investments, uncertain). Shares fell 8.1% from 11-04 to 11-06 after the Q3 10-Q, cause not established. Now read: 58.8% combined ratio reflects zero cat losses and favorable prior-year development; reserve roll-forward shows 145M of reductions on prior and cat years (not all development) against 342.7M 9M pre-tax income, so earnings are likely flattered by a benign year. Cash fell mainly because 752.8M went into securities, not a loss of liquidity. Reinsurance recoverable is concentrated (five reinsurers 64.1%).
invalidation: Large Florida hurricane loss or reinsurance tower failure, adverse reserve development, Florida market softening that lowers premiums and margins, or evidence that 2026 earnings were boosted by unusually light cat losses or reserve releases.
